title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-26
content:
2026-03-03 | quick scratchpad - GPU ops / capacity / networking

Top of mind:
- Ramp plan for Q2: target +15% baseline capacity for inference clusters (predictable burst). check reserved node pools and billing impact.
- Follow up with finance on cost model change (estimate hourly GPU cost w/ batching improvements).

TODAY
- Check node health across us-west1-gpu-pool: kubectl get nodes -o wide -> look for Ready=Unknown or NotReady.
- Validate MIG partitioning after driver update (NVIDIA 535.x) on prod-gpu-3. One node reported OOMs during long seq tests.
- Run quick perf run for rtx-a6000 with 32k context (sample workload) on staging to validate kernel selection (latency + throughput).
- Confirm autoscaler config: targetUtilization 0.75 -> maybe lower to 0.7 for steady tail latency.

Commands/notes to self:
- k get pods -n infra -l app=gpu-metrics --field-selector=status.phase!=Running
- ssh ops@gpu-host-12 -> journalctl -u nvidia-driver.service -n 200
- nvidia-smi topo --matrix (verify NVLink across hosts before large batch jobs)
- check /var/log/kubelet.log for segfault-like errors around 2026-03-02 14:00 UTC (ticket INFRA-2471)

Incident follow-ups:
- INFRA-2471: transient OOM spikes on prod-gpu-3 during long-context evals. Root cause hypothesis: KV cache accumulation + incorrect early eviction. Need to repro on staging with same workload. Rajiv to send exact trace.
- Action: add additional max-kv-cache-size env override for inference runtime in staging, run 3x long seq jobs overnight.

Capacity planning notes:
- Current committed nodes: 120 GPUs (mixed A100 & A10G). Q2 demand forecast +18% from ML teams. Suggested options:
  1) Move 10 A10G -> A100 (if available) for high-memory jobs.
  2) Reserve 8 extra burst nodes in us-east for low-latency customers.
  3) Improve prefix caching (reduce per-token compute) -> estimated 9% cost reduction.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Check if kernel 6.4.x regression affects rpc timeouts on some nodes (SRE thread).
- Confirm whether autoscaler cooldown is working with fast-scaling workloads (reports of slow scale-up).
- Schedule 1:1 with Sofia to review rollout plan for driver update (post-mortem action).

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep short-lived spot pools for batch evals; ensure fallback to on-demand after 10m of pod pending.
- Add canary for model-variant fallback policy to avoid full outage when a large model is evicted.
- Update runbook: add explicit step for "clear KV cache" before heavy long-seq tests. Add link to runbook PR once merged.

Links / refs:
- Perf run notebook (staging): /notebooks/perf/long-context-a6000-32k.ipynb (ask Rajiv for copy)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/512 (autoscaler tweak)
- Jira: INFRA-2471 (OOM spikes)

End-of-day quick checklist:
- [ ] Confirm staging repro for INFRA-2471
- [ ] Merge autoscaler tweak PR if staging good
- [ ] Sync with finance + product on Q2 capacity commit
- [ ] Send driver upgrade status update to #infra-alerts

Random brain dump (notes to self):
- If we can get ~10% perf uplift from kernel-level GEMM tuning, that beats adding 6 GPUs. Worth setting up small benchmark.
- Consider adding a nightly cron job that collects nvtop + gpu metrics into a short perf archive for debugging.

-- Lena M.
